title: Smart Routing: policy-configured fallback model/region when overload triggers
creator: Mina Haddad
project: Reliability Program: Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding
description:
Goal
Implement safe, policy-configurable fallback routing (model and/or region) when overload protection triggers (breaker open / admission shed) so we degrade predictably instead of timing out or causing retries to pile up.

Context
During burst traffic and partial regional saturation, the gateway/runtime will begin shedding. For tenants that have opted in, Smart Routing should be able to:
- route a request to a compatible fallback model variant in the same region, or
- route to the same model in an alternate region (if allowed by tenant policy + residency), or
- fall back to a compatible model in an alternate region (strictest constraints)
…without creating retry storms, routing loops, or breaking compatibility guarantees.

Non-goals (for this ticket)
- Building a new model-compatibility service (use existing model catalog compatibility tags + conservative gating).
- Cross-cloud provider brokering beyond current multi-region primitives.
- Changing SDK behavior (handled in ENG-4832 / SDK PRs).

Design references
- ADR-015: Admission control layering (gateway vs routing vs runtime)
- ADR-014: Overload error taxonomy + Retry-After semantics

Proposed behavior (high level)
1) If the primary candidate route fails with an overload condition (internal reason maps to stable overload error codes) OR if the gateway signals breaker-open for that route/model, Smart Routing evaluates tenant policy for fallback eligibility.
2) If eligible, attempt exactly one fallback plan (bounded) according to configured precedence:
   a) same region, fallback model (preferred)
   b) fallback region, same model
   c) fallback region + fallback model (only if explicitly configured)
3) If fallback is not allowed or fails with overload too, return the original overload response (do not fan out multiple fallbacks).

Safety constraints / guardrails (must-have)
- Loop prevention:
  - Annotate requests with an internal routing header (e.g., x-rw-fallback-attempt: 0|1) and a chosen candidate fingerprint.
  - If x-rw-fallback-attempt >= 1, do not attempt fallback again.
  - Ensure no cycles in policy graph (validate at policy load time; fail-closed to no-fallback).
- Bounded retries:
  - Max 1 fallback attempt per request.
  - Do not fallback on non-overload errors (e.g., 4xx auth, 5xx non-overload, upstream validation errors).
- Residency / compliance:
  - Region fallback requires tenant allowlist (explicit), and only among approved regions for that tenant.
  - Dedicated/isolated tiers: do not route across isolation boundaries (Hosted → Dedicated, Dedicated → Hosted is forbidden).
- Compatibility gating:
  - Only fallback to models marked “compatible_variant=true” with the original route’s API semantics (chat vs completions; tool calling/JSON mode constraints).
  - For streaming requests: fallback allowed, but must preserve stream semantics and correlation IDs; do not downgrade streaming to non-streaming.
  - If request requires features not supported on fallback model (tools/structured output), do not fallback unless a degradation flag is explicitly enabled by policy (PM-1191 governs allowed degradations).
- Observability:
  - Emit routing outcome metric labels with bounded cardinality: primary_model, fallback_model (if any), primary_region, fallback_region, reason (enum), and tenant_tier (enum). Avoid tenant_id as a label.
  - Preserve request correlation ID and append routing decision to structured logs.

Acceptance criteria
- Functional
  - When overload triggers for primary candidate, eligible tenants are routed to fallback candidate per policy precedence.
  - Fallback attempt is bounded to 1 and is loop-safe.
  - If fallback is not eligible or not available, response returns the canonical overload error payload (ADR-014) with Retry-After and correlation ID.
- Policy
  - Policy engine can express fallback model/region mapping with safe defaults (no-fallback unless explicitly enabled).
  - Invalid policies (cycles, disallowed regions) are rejected at validation time; system continues with safe default behavior.
- Metrics
  - We can graph: fallback_attempt_rate, fallback_success_rate, and “overload_error_rate without fallback” vs “with fallback” during canary.
  - No significant increase in downstream saturation due to fallback (monitor queue depth & shed rate in target region).

Implementation plan
- Routing layer
  - Add “fallback plan” evaluation step when overload signal is detected.
  - Encode routing attempt metadata in internal headers (strip at edge).
  - Implement candidate selection with strict ordering and stop conditions.
- Policy integration
  - Read new policy fields from overload policy engine (Jordan/Benji hooks) and cache per-tenant + per-route.
  - Add policy validation hooks: cycle detection + region allowlist enforcement.
- Compatibility
  - Use model catalog compatibility tags (existing) and enforce feature requirements (tools/structured output) before selecting fallback model.
- Telemetry
  - Metrics + structured logs + tracing span annotations.

Testing
- Unit tests
  - Loop prevention (header present / multiple attempts)
  - Non-overload errors do not trigger fallback
  - Region disallowed → no fallback
  - Feature mismatch prevents fallback
- Integration tests (perf-canary)
  - Burst traffic scenario triggers breaker → observe fallback to configured candidate
  - Confirm bounded retries (no multi-hop)
- Failure-mode tests
  - Fallback region also overloaded: ensure we return overload response quickly (no added tail latency)

Rollout
- Dark launch
  - Ship code paths off by default; enable metrics for “would have fallen back” decisions.
- Canary
  - Enable for 1 region (us-east) and small tenant allowlist (SRE-approved).
  - Gate on: p95/p99 latency, shed rate, fallback success rate, and error budget burn.
- Progressive rollout
  - Expand tenants + regions after 48–72h stable; rollback if: fallback causes >X% increase in shed rate in target region or creates elevated 5xx.

Open questions
- Do we allow fallback on “dependency brownout” (e.g., tokenizer service)? Initial proposal: NO for this ticket; only overload/breaker-open.
- How to represent “compatible variant” for tool-calling routes where schema differs? Proposal: disallow by default; require explicit degradation allow.

Links
- Epic: ENG-4821 Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding
- Error taxonomy: ENG-4822 (ADR-014)
- Gateway admission control: ENG-4823
- Runtime saturation signals: ENG-4825
- PR (planned/track): PR-18458 Smart Routing fallback when breaker open

comments: 2025-11-08 (Mina Haddad): Marking P0. We should treat fallback as a safety valve during canary, but only with strict bounds (1 attempt, no loops). Please align with ADR-015 layering so we don’t create feedback loops with gateway/runtime shedding.

2025-11-12 (Peter Holtz): +1 on bounded attempt. Strong preference for metric dimensions that avoid tenant_id. We need a clean enum for reason: breaker_open | runtime_shed | gateway_shed | capacity_signal. Also confirm we do NOT fallback on generic 5xx.

2025-11-14 (Elena Popov): Drafted routing header plan: x-rw-fallback-attempt + x-rw-route-fingerprint. Will ensure headers are stripped at edge. Adding a validation check to reject policies that create cycles (A->B and B->A).

2025-11-18 (Rafael Mendes): For canary, SRE wants explicit rollback trigger: fallback_attempt_rate > 5% AND fallback_success_rate < 60% for 30m OR shed_rate increases > 15% in fallback region. Also require we preserve Retry-After semantics from ADR-014 even if fallback fails.

2025-11-21 (Jordan Lee): Policy engine can expose fallback config under overload policy namespace. Validation can include region allowlist and a simple DAG check per-tenant policy set. Need final field names from routing by EOW.

2025-11-26 (Elena Popov): Implemented candidate selection ordering (same region/model-variant first). Added compatibility gating for route type (chat/completions) and tool-calling requirement. Still need to wire runtime overload reason mapping to routing decision (waiting on ENG-4825 signal naming).

2025-11-28 (Mina Haddad): Please ensure we don’t degrade features implicitly. If tools/structured output requested and fallback lacks support, fail closed (no fallback) unless PM-1191 explicitly allows that degradation mode for the tenant.
